what_it_checks: torch replay of the kernel's exact flat-pointer arithmetic vs level 3, float64, 7 cases
backend_tested: neither (emulates the Triton kernel's indexing in torch; no Triton is imported)
measured_result: worst over all 7 cases = 1.42e-14 (dg, dense R=3). Cases: dense R1/R2/R3, ragged K, ragged V, initial_state, varlen. ALL PASS
notes: This is the level that validates the OFFSET ARITHMETIC, and it is the strongest link in the chain. I verified the offsets are LITERALLY THE SAME EXPRESSIONS as the kernel's: e.g. the emulator's dq store index `i_v * s_dq + ((bos + t) * H + i_h) * K + o_k` (bwd_emulator.py:223) is character-for-character the kernel's `p_dq` arithmetic (kda_householder.py:407), and dk/db/hs match likewise. TWO STRUCTURAL CAVEATS THE WRITE-UP SHOULD STATE: (a) it is an emulator, so it can only catch indexing bugs the emulator does not itself share with the kernel -- a shared misconception is invisible to this level by construction; (b) **THE EMULATOR IMPLEMENTS A DIFFERENT R-CHAIN STRATEGY THAN THE SHIPPED KERNEL.** The emulator stores R+1 tiles in an `inner` list (bwd_emulator.py:209-218); the kernel instead re-walks from S^(0) for each r, O(R^2) with two live tiles (kda_householder.py:440-449), precisely to avoid register spills at BK=128. So level 4 did NOT validate the code path that actually ships. That gap is exactly what audit_exp6_rewalk.py exists to close, and it does close it (bit-identical, R up to 8, reproduced by me). The chain is sound only when levels 4 and exp6 are cited TOGETHER; level 4 alone is insufficient.
